# spawnBayes

`spawnBayes` estimates salmon spawner abundance and run timing from
repeated live-count surveys.Unlike traditional area-under-the-curve
(TAUC) approaches, `spawnBayes` jointly estimates abundance, run timing,
effective residence time, and associated uncertainty using a
hierarchical Bayesian model.

The package supports analyses of individual streams as well as
integrated analyses across multiple groups. Groups may represent
reaches, streams, rivers, populations, index areas, or other
biologically meaningful assessment units. In multi-group analyses,
timing information is shared among groups while abundance is estimated
separately for each group.

The package is designed to support salmon stock assessment and
escapement monitoring programs. Users provide survey dates and spawner
counts and obtain estimates of annual abundance, run timing, effective
residence time, and associated uncertainty.

## Documentation

Online documentation, function reference pages, and worked tutorials are
available at:

[spawnBayes documentation](https://sire-p.github.io/spawnBayes/)

## Installation

``` r
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("SiRE-P/spawnBayes")
```

## Prerequisites

`spawnBayes` uses `cmdstanr` and requires a local installation of
CmdStan.

Install `cmdstanr`:

``` r
install.packages(
  "cmdstanr",
  repos = c(
    "https://mc-stan.org/r-packages/",
    getOption("repos")
  )
)
```

Then follow the official CmdStan installation guide:

<https://mc-stan.org/docs/cmdstan-guide/installation.html>

Verify the installation:

``` r
cmdstanr::cmdstan_version()
```

## Data Requirements

Required columns:

| Variable         | Description                      |
|------------------|----------------------------------|
| `date`           | Survey date                      |
| `spawner_counts` | Number of live spawners observed |

Optional columns:

| Variable | Description |
|----|----|
| `group` | Group identifier (reach, stream, river, population, index area, etc.) |
| `observer_efficiency` | Proportion of fish detected during a survey (0-1) |
| `coverage` | Proportion of spawning habitat surveyed (0-1) |
| `survey_error_group` | Observation-error category used to estimate group-specific observation dispersion |

If `group` is omitted, all observations are assumed to belong to a
single group.

If `observer_efficiency` or `coverage` are omitted, values of 1 are
assumed.

If `survey_error_group` is omitted, all observations are assumed to
share a common observation-error distribution.

## What Is a Group?

A group is the unit for which abundance is estimated and timing is
allowed to vary independently.

Groups may represent:

- stream reaches
- streams
- rivers
- populations
- index areas
- other biologically meaningful assessment units

Single-group analyses estimate abundance for one group. Multi-group
analyses share timing information among groups while estimating
abundance separately for each group.

In general, groups should be analysed together when they are expected to
share broad seasonal timing patterns and survey information from one
group may help inform timing estimates in another.

Groups may be analysed separately or jointly. When in doubt, fitting
both a single-group and multi-group model can help assess whether shared
timing information improves inference.

## Tutorials

The package includes three worked tutorials:

### Getting Started with spawnBayes

Learn how to fit and interpret a single-population model using Artlish
River Chinook salmon data.

[Getting Started with
spawnBayes](https://sire-p.github.io/spawnBayes/articles/getting-started.md)

### Multi-Population Analyses in spawnBayes

Fit multiple rivers jointly and share timing information among groups
while estimating abundance separately for each population.

[Multi-Population Analyses in
spawnBayes](https://sire-p.github.io/spawnBayes/articles/multi-population.md)

### Importing NuSEDS Data into spawnBayes

Learn how to export data from NuSEDS and import it directly into
`spawnBayes` using
[`read_nuseds()`](https://sire-p.github.io/spawnBayes/reference/read_nuseds.md).

[Importing NuSEDS Data into
spawnBayes](https://sire-p.github.io/spawnBayes/articles/importing-nuseds.md)

## Data Template

Create a template CSV file in the current working directory:

``` r
template_file()
```

This creates:

``` text
spawnBayes_template.csv
```

containing the required and optional input columns.

## Citation

If you use `spawnBayes` in a publication, please cite:

Thompson, P. L., Akenhead, S. A., and Louie, C. (2026). *Estimating
spawning salmon abundance from visual surveys: a hierarchical model of
arrival and exit dynamics*. Canadian Journal of Fisheries and Aquatic
Sciences, 83, 1-13. <https://doi.org/10.1139/cjfas-2026-0029>

# Package index

## All functions

- [`abundance()`](https://sire-p.github.io/spawnBayes/reference/abundance.md)
  : Extract abundance estimates
- [`clemens_sockeye`](https://sire-p.github.io/spawnBayes/reference/clemens_sockeye.md)
  : Clemens Creek sockeye survey data
- [`default_priors()`](https://sire-p.github.io/spawnBayes/reference/default_priors.md)
  : Default prior specification
- [`diagnostics()`](https://sire-p.github.io/spawnBayes/reference/diagnostics.md)
  : Summarize model diagnostics
- [`fit_spawner()`](https://sire-p.github.io/spawnBayes/reference/fit_spawner.md)
  : Fit a spawner abundance model
- [`nvi_chinook`](https://sire-p.github.io/spawnBayes/reference/nvi_chinook.md)
  : Northwest Vancouver Island Chinook spawner survey data
- [`plot_abundance()`](https://sire-p.github.io/spawnBayes/reference/plot_abundance.md)
  : Plot abundance estimates
- [`plot_nuseds()`](https://sire-p.github.io/spawnBayes/reference/plot_nuseds.md)
  : Plot imported NuSEDS survey data
- [`plot_run_curve()`](https://sire-p.github.io/spawnBayes/reference/plot_run_curve.md)
  : Plot fitted run curves
- [`plot_timing()`](https://sire-p.github.io/spawnBayes/reference/plot_timing.md)
  : Plot timing estimates
- [`prior_post_plot()`](https://sire-p.github.io/spawnBayes/reference/prior_post_plot.md)
  : Plot prior and posterior distributions
- [`read_nuseds()`](https://sire-p.github.io/spawnBayes/reference/read_nuseds.md)
  : Import NuSEDS stream inspection log exports
- [`template_file()`](https://sire-p.github.io/spawnBayes/reference/template_file.md)
  : Create a spawnBayes data template
- [`timing()`](https://sire-p.github.io/spawnBayes/reference/timing.md)
  : Extract timing estimates
- [`validate_data()`](https://sire-p.github.io/spawnBayes/reference/validate_data.md)
  : Validate spawnBayes input data
